Rule and exact checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

Claimed finding status: deviation

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"preferred","mappings":[{"element":"Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]}]}

Finding rationale:
Section 11.1 commits Corio to an initial five-year term with automatic one-year renewals, and Section 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. No convenience exit exists for Corio anywhere in the Agreement (the exits at p0050 and p0079 are acceptance-test and warranty remedies), so the bargain fails even the fallback, which requires a Customer convenience right on 60-90 days' notice. The 30-day non-renewal notice in 11.1 is a natural-term non-renewal mechanic under RENEWAL, not a Vendor mid-term convenience right, so it is not flagged here. We therefore insert Section 11.4 carrying the four preferred elements: Corio (identified expressly as Commerce One's customer, since "CUSTOMER(S)" is defined in Section 1.6 as Corio's own customers) may terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice, Commerce One refunds prepaid fees pro rata, and Commerce One has no convenience right during the initial or renewal terms. The section number is embedded so the survival list and cross-references remain clean, and no partial-termination language is added because there is no Order Form structure.

Original cited paragraphs:
p0096: 11.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years. Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
p0097: 11.2 Termination. If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period. This Agreement shall terminate immediately upon notice if either party becomes insolvent (i.e., becomes unable to pay its debts in the ordinary course of business as they come due) or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors. Compliance by the Software with the Software's specifications after expiration of the Warranty Period shall be deemed a material condition of this Agreement.

Resolved definitions:
SOFTWARE: 1.10 "SOFTWARE" means Commerce One's proprietary software described in EXHIBIT A attached hereto and made a part hereof, in object code form only, and any Updates or Upgrades (as defined below) thereto.
Warranty Period: 7.3 Product Warranty. Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation, and the media on which the Software is distributed will be free from defects in materials and workmanship under normal use, for a period of sixty (60) days from the Effective Date, but in no event not later than December 31, 1999 (the "Warranty Period"). In addition, Commerce One warrants that during the Warranty Period the Software and MarketSite.net Service is free of any willfully introduced computer virus, or any other similar harmful, malicious or hidden program or data, which is designed to disable, erase, or alter the Software, or any other files, data, or software.

Rendered operative language:
11.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years. Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.
11.2 Termination. If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period. This Agreement shall terminate immediately upon notice if either party becomes insolvent (i.e., becomes unable to pay its debts in the ordinary course of business as they come due) or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors. Compliance by the Software with the Software's specifications after expiration of the Warranty Period shall be deemed a material condition of this Agreement.
11.3 Effect of Termination. The following Sections shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason: 4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 14. Corio's right to allow its then-existing Customers and their Software Users to use and access the Software in accordance with Section 2 of this Agreement and all payment obligations related thereto shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement. Commerce One's obligation to provide Software support and maintenance to Corio and its Customers shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement, provided Corio continues to make its annual support and maintenance payments as specified in this Agreement. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.
11.4 Termination for Convenience. Corio, as Commerce One's customer under this Agreement, may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One, in which case Commerce One shall refund pro rata any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term.

Margin comment:
[Playbook] Section 11 leaves us with no convenience exit across a five-year committed term, so we have added Section 11.4 allowing Corio, as Commerce One's customer, to terminate on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirming Commerce One has no convenience right during the initial or renewal terms. We can move to 60-90 days' notice as a fallback if needed.

content.text: No liquidated damages, penalties, early-termination fees, late-payment charges or shortfall payments payable by Corio appear anywhere (Sections 4, 9, 11, 13, 17, Exhibit B). Submitting as compliant at the preferred level.

input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages or penalties on Corio (our client, the customer/licensee), so it meets the preferred position. Corio's monetary obligations are limited to actual fees for value received: license fees (4.1), annual maintenance and support fees (4.2), taxes (4.3), revenue-sharing and implementation fees (Exhibit B) and standard fees for optional shared resources (13.1-13.2), all payable on the ordinary net-30/acceptance terms in Exhibit B's Payment Terms. Termination (11.1-11.2) is by non-renewal notice or for uncured material breach or insolvency, with no early-termination fee, minimum-fee shortfall, acceleration of remaining contract value or forfeiture on termination; post-termination payments under 11.3 are only continuing support/maintenance fees for services Corio elects to keep receiving. Section 9 further caps each party's liability at amounts actually paid by Corio, reinforcing that no stipulated or penal sum runs against us. The only true-up mechanics are the audit provisions in 4.4 (payment of an actual shortfall and reimbursement of examination cost on a >5% underpayment), which are compensatory audit terms rather than liquidated damages, and we note them for information only. No fallback early-termination-fee cap is needed because no Customer-payable liquidated amount exists.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.",
  "Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.",
  "Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.",
  "If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.",
  "Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.",
  "Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.",
  "Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000."
]

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Retained text reads "Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year". A calendar-year cap is not a rolling 12-month cap: a December inspection and a following January inspection are both permitted. To meet the preferred element the drafter would need "no more than once in any twelve (12) month period".

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The edit inserts "upon at least 15 days' notice" — half the preferred quantum, and it is not expressed as written notice.

elements.element: Audits occur during business hours.
elements.evidence: Clause says only "at reasonable times"; no express business-hours limitation was added.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: "open for inspection by an independent certified public accountant reasonably acceptable to Corio" — independent third-party auditor, subject to Customer's reasonable acceptance.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 4.4 contains no confidentiality undertaking from or in respect of the accountant, and the redline adds none; no non-disclosure obligation is imposed on the auditor in operative language.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No location/off-site language appears in the rendered clause; the books are simply "open for inspection".

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection", with reimbursement by Corio only "if any such inspection reveals an underpayment of more than five percent (5%) for the period under audit" — exactly the preferred cost allocation and threshold.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The right is confined to inspection of "books of accounts and records for determining the amounts payable" by an accountant; no remote or direct system-access right is granted anywhere in the clause, so the walk-away trigger is absent.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Retained: "Such inspections may be made no more than once each calendar year" — an express annual frequency cap satisfying the fallback (which does not require a rolling 12-month measure).

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 replaces open-ended "reasonable notice" with "upon at least 15 days' notice", fixing a hard minimum notice period exactly at the fallback quantum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall bear all costs and expenses of such inspection", with cost-shifting only on an underpayment "of more than five percent (5%)". Vendor-borne cost is expressly allocated and the shifting trigger is the 5% figure the playbook itself specifies at the preferred level, so the cost-allocation element is satisfied; note the retained 5% (rather than 10%) trigger shifts cost to Customer somewhat sooner than the fallback figure if the team wants to press it.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: frequency (once each calendar year) and Vendor-borne cost with a 5% underpayment trigger were already in Section 4.4, and the single gap — an indeterminate "reasonable notice" with no floor — is closed by the inserted "at least 15 days' notice".

Preferred level is not reached: notice is 15 rather than 30 days and not stated to be written; there is no business-hours limitation (only "at reasonable times"), no off-site preference, no auditor confidentiality undertaking, and the frequency cap is calendar-year rather than any rolling 12-month period. These are correctly noted rather than pressed, but the level must not be marked complete.

Minimal: exactly one phrase is changed within the notice element ("upon reasonable notice" -> "upon at least 15 days' notice"). Favourable retained language — annual cap, independent CPA reasonably acceptable to Customer, Vendor cost-bearing, books-and-records-only scope, the reciprocal shortfall/overpayment true-up and the 3-year retention period — is untouched, and no survival tail, procedure or extra requirement outside the checklist is added.

Preserves intent: the audit's purpose (verifying amounts payable), the reciprocal payment/refund mechanic and the 5% reimbursement trigger all survive without contradiction; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created, and "at reasonable times" still coexists coherently with the new fixed notice period.

Optional hardening if the counterparty engages: add "written" before notice and, if the team wants literal fallback parity on cost, raise the reimbursement trigger from 5% to 10%; neither is required for fallback completeness as scored here.

Severity is reduced to low: the clause sat at or above the fallback on every material term except the notice floor, and the walk-away triggers (unlimited/unannounced audits, system access) were never present.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 7.3 as rendered warrants only substantial conformance of the Software and MarketSite.net Service to the Documentation and defect-free media; no professional/workmanlike standard of performance appears anywhere in the rendered language, and the redline did not add one.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One warrants that the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation"; "Software" and "Documentation" are both defined terms.

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Rendered period is "ninety (90) days from the Effective Date (the \"Warranty Period\")" — well short of 12 months; the drafter expressly declined to seek the preferred period.

elements.element: The Services warranty lasts 90 days.
elements.evidence: The single Warranty Period of ninety (90) days covers the MarketSite.net Service as well as the Software.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One shall take all commercially reasonable efforts to correct the Software and MarketSite.net Service, or if correction ... is reasonably not possible, replace such Software and MarketSite.net Service free of charge."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include a refund.
elements.evidence: "In the event any such breach of warranty can not be reasonably corrected at Commerce One's sole expense, Corio has the right to terminate this Agreement and receive a refund of all prepaid fees."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered Section 7.3/7.4 language; none was added.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: "Commerce One warrants that during the Warranty Period the Software and MarketSite.net Service is free of any willfully introduced computer virus, or any other similar harmful, malicious or hidden program or data..." (limited to the Warranty Period, but the no-malicious-code warranty is expressly present).

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "the Software and MarketSite.net Service will perform in substantial accordance with the Documentation ... for a period of ninety (90) days from the Effective Date (the \"Warranty Period\")". The December 31, 1999 outside date that would have truncated the 90 days (90 days from the 29 October 1999 Effective Date runs to late January 2000) has been deleted, so the full 90 days survives.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: The MarketSite.net Service is covered by the same conformance warranty and the same ninety (90) day Warranty Period, exceeding the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Retained: commercially reasonable efforts to correct, and free-of-charge replacement where correction is not reasonably possible; defective media also replaced.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include a refund.
elements.evidence: Retained: termination plus "a refund of all prepaid fees" where the breach cannot reasonably be corrected — a refund remedy is available on breach of the conformance warranty.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative rendered text: 90-day Software-to-Documentation warranty, the same 90-day period for the MarketSite.net Service (above the 30-day floor), correction/free replacement, and a refund of all prepaid fees.

Preferred level is not reached: no professional-and-workmanlike services standard, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months. These are noted, not required, because the fallback is complete.

Minimality holds. Only two edits were made inside the target element: sixty (60) → ninety (90), and deletion of "but in no event not later than December 31, 1999". The outside date deletion is necessary rather than cosmetic — with an Effective Date of 29 October 1999, a 31 December 1999 cap would have cut the period to roughly 63 days and contradicted the extension. No survival tail, expense language, extra remedies or boilerplate were added.

Intent is preserved. The defined term "Warranty Period" is retained and still anchors the malicious-code warranty, the media-replacement sentence, the correction/refund cascade, the sole-and-exclusive-remedies sentence and the exclusions list; no cross-reference is left dangling and no retained sentence now contradicts the 90-day period.

The underlying finding of deviation is correct: at 60 days (further truncated by the 31 December 1999 cap) the original Software conformance warranty fell below the 90-day fallback floor, which is a material term rather than a minor sub-element.

Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.",
  "Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.",
  "Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.",
  "Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty."
]

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Section 11.4: "Corio, as Commerce One's customer under this Agreement, may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One". The element is disjunctive (Agreement or Order Form) and this contract has no Order Form structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: 11.4 requires "thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One" — exactly the 30-day ceiling, in writing, running from Customer's notice.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 11.4: "Commerce One shall refund pro rata any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination." The words "pro rata" are express, not merely inferred from a post-termination period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: 11.4: "Commerce One shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial five (5) year term or any renewal term." Retained 11.2 gives Commerce One only for-cause/insolvency exits, and the 30-day notice in 11.1 is a natural-term non-renewal tied to expiration of the then-current term (RENEWAL, not mid-term T4C), so no retained sentence contradicts 11.4.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 11.4 sets thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (it is the preferred, more Customer-favourable figure).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty, or accelerated-payment mechanic is imposed anywhere in Section 11 or in the inserted 11.4, so the three-month ceiling is satisfied a fortiori.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply in a stricter form: 11.4 gives Commerce One no convenience right at all during the initial or any renewal term, and 11.1's non-renewal notice operates only at expiration of the then-current term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Commerce One has no convenience termination right to exercise under 11.4, so no notice floor is triggered; the 30-day notice in 11.1 is a natural-term non-renewal mechanic assessed under RENEWAL.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the inserted Section 11.4 carries all four preferred elements (Customer convenience right, 30 days' written notice, express pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during the initial and renewal terms).

The 'Customer convenience termination present' regex returning false reflects the baseline document (and the fact that the Customer is named 'Corio' rather than a playbook alias); inspected in substance, the rendered 11.4 plainly grants Corio a convenience exit, so the mechanical miss does not defeat coverage.

Minimality holds: existing 11.1–11.3 are untouched, no favourable language is deleted, the model-language surplus 'in whole or in part' was correctly omitted because there is no Order Form or partial-termination structure, and no survival tail, expense, or procedural extras were added. The short appositive 'as Commerce One's customer under this Agreement' is a lowercase descriptor that does not invoke the defined term CUSTOMER(S) in Section 1.6 and imposes no operative requirement; it is at most cosmetic.

Intent preserved: Section 11.3's survival list (4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14) and the Corio Customer/support carve-outs continue to operate on any termination including one under 11.4; the new section number 11.4 creates no dangling cross-reference and no retained sentence contradicts the new right.

Fallback is not independently complete because notice is 30 days rather than 60–90, but that is irrelevant to position-completeness since the preferred checklist is fully met; the comment's offer to move to 60–90 days is a negotiation concession, not an operative gap.
Finding status 'deviation' is correct: the original Section 11 gave Corio no convenience exit across a five-year committed term, failing even the fallback.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

The 30-day non-renewal notice in 11.1 is a natural-term non-renewal mechanic under RENEWAL, not a Vendor mid-term convenience right, so we do not flag it here. We therefore add the preferred package: Corio convenience termination on 30 days' notice with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees, plus confirmation that Commerce One has no convenience right during the committed or renewal terms. No Order Form structure exists, so no partial-termination language was added.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: T4C — deviation (high).**

- **What the document does:** Section 11.1 commits Corio to an initial five-year term with automatic one-year renewals; Section 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency. No convenience right exists for either party anywhere in the Agreement (the p0050 acceptance-test exit and p0079 warranty exit are conditional remedies, not convenience rights).
- **Why it fails fallback:** The fallback requires a Customer convenience right on 60–90 days' notice; here Corio has none at all in a multi-year committed term, which is the walk-away scenario in the playbook.
- **Not double-flagged:** The 30-day non-renewal notice in 11.1 is natural-term non-renewal (RENEWAL), not a Vendor mid-term convenience right.
- **Cure (preferred, one insertion as new 11.4):** Corio convenience termination on 30 days' written notice, pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Commerce One convenience termination during the initial or renewal terms. No partial-termination or Order Form language was added, since this contract has no Order Form structure.

**Finding: LD — compliant (preferred level).**

The Agreement contains no liquidated damages or penalty payable by Corio, our client:

- **Fees (§4, Exhibit B/Payment Terms):** only actual consideration — license fees, annual maintenance and support, taxes, revenue-sharing, implementation on time-and-materials with a cap, and optional shared-resource fees. No late-payment interest or penalty charge.
- **Term and termination (§11):** termination by non-renewal notice, uncured material breach, or insolvency. No early-termination fee, no minimum-fee shortfall, no acceleration of remaining contract value, no forfeiture. Post-termination payments in §11.3 are only ongoing support/maintenance fees for services Corio elects to continue receiving.
- **Limitation of liability (§9):** caps each party's liability at amounts actually paid by Corio, further confirming no stipulated penal sum runs against us.
- **Noted for information only (not a deviation):** §4.4 audit true-up requires payment of an actual shortfall and reimbursement of examination cost on a >5% underpayment. These are compensatory audit mechanics, not liquidated damages, and the shortfall is by definition an amount genuinely owed.

Because the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) is already satisfied, no redline was proposed and the fallback three-month early-termination-fee cap is unnecessary.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

paragraphs.text: 11 TERM AND TERMINATION.

11.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and shall continue in full force and effect for an initial period of five (5) years. Thereafter, this Agreement shall automatically renew for subsequent one (1) year periods unless either party provides the other party with written notification at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal thereof of its intention to terminate this Agreement.

11.2 Termination. If either party materially breaches any term or condition of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within-thirty (30) days after receiving written notice of the breach, the nonbreaching party may terminate this Agreement on written notice at any time following the end of such-thirty (30) day period. This Agreement shall terminate immediately upon notice if either party becomes insolvent (i.e., becomes unable to pay its debts in the ordinary course of business as they come due) or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors. Compliance by the Software with the Software's specifications after expiration of the Warranty Period shall be deemed a material condition of this Agreement.

11.3 Effect of Termination. The following Sections shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason: 4.2, 5.3, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 14. Corio's right to allow its then-existing Customers and their Software Users to use and access the Software in accordance with Section 2 of this Agreement and all payment obligations related thereto shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement. Commerce One's obligation to provide Software support and maintenance to Corio and its Customers shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement, provided Corio continues to make its annual support and maintenance payments as specified in this Agreement. Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, each party shall otherwise return or destroy any Confidential Information of the other party provided, however, Corio may retain any Confidential Information necessary for Corio to continue supporting it's then-existing Customers.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Corio Inc.; counterparty is Commerce One, Inc..

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]
