system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.",
  "Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.",
  "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.",
  "Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.",
  "Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.",
  "Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.",
  "Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination."
]

You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-bb81c8fa","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8 INDEMNIFICATION.","rationale":"Section 8.1 gives Corio (and its Customers) a Commerce One defence-and-indemnity for third-party claims that the Software infringes patent, copyright, trademark or trade secret rights, with the usual notice, tender-of-control and cooperation mechanics, and the standard remedy ladder: procure the right to continue use, replace or modify to make the Software non-infringing, failing which termination and a pro-rated refund of fees paid (p0086-p0087). Section 8.2 keeps exclusions narrow (use outside the Documentation and third-party modification), so there are no combination or specification carve-outs — that omission favours us and is not a deviation, since those exclusions are only permitted, not required, at the fallback. On the super-cap element, Section 9 expressly excepts \"LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8\" from the 12-month fee cap, so the indemnity is uncapped — better for us than the 3x annual fees super-cap the fallback allows. The clause therefore sits at the fallback position and is acceptable as drafted. It does not reach preferred because the indemnity is IP-only (no heads for Commerce One's breach of applicable law, a Commerce One-caused data breach, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and defence control sits wholly with Commerce One. There is no Corio-side indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, so the narrow-Customer-indemnity concern does not arise. These are preferred-only gaps, noted rather than redlined.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-598bd48e","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13 SHARED RESOURCES.","rationale":"Section 13.5 gives Corio ownership of the Developments it creates and includes a Commerce One assignment and a pre-existing IP reservation, but it reverses direction whenever Commerce One supports the Developments on an ongoing basis: Commerce One then retains all ownership rights in Corio-created work product with no licence back. That is walk-away territory (assignment of Customer IP to Vendor) and fails the fallback as well, since Corio receives no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to the work product it loses. There is also no licence to Commerce One IP embedded in the Developments, no statement that Corio's data remains Corio's (Commerce One processes data through the MarketSite.net Service and support), and ownership of jointly developed Software enhancements is left open. We have therefore made the shortest edits at the preferred level: delete the ownership-reversal carve-out, add a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free embedded-IP licence and a Corio data-ownership sentence limiting Commerce One's use to providing the Software and services, and confirm that no IP is jointly owned.","proposal":"Corio owns Developments outright; add embedded-IP licence back, Corio data ownership, and no joint ownership","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-22ed87d4","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"SALES AND MARKETING COOPERATION","rationale":"We reviewed every candidate hook and found no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Corio. The Section 2 grants run in Corio's favour and are all \"nonexclusive\" (Sections 2.1-2.4), Section 2.4 in fact restricts Commerce One from approaching Corio Customers directly; nothing obliges Corio to source procurement software or hosting content solely from Commerce One, to lead with the Software, or to refrain from third-party products. The CORIO MARKET SEGMENT and TERRITORY definitions only scope where and to whom the licences may be exercised; they impose no purchasing commitment. Exhibit D (Sales and Marketing Cooperation) is expressly non-binding and contains only cross-selling and joint-marketing aspirations, and Exhibit B's revenue share is a fee mechanic rather than a requirements commitment. This meets the preferred position, so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-0a8ff0a0","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages or penalties on Corio (our client, the customer/licensee), so it meets the preferred position. Corio's monetary obligations are limited to actual fees for value received: license fees (4.1), annual maintenance and support fees (4.2), taxes (4.3), revenue-sharing and implementation fees (Exhibit B) and standard fees for optional shared resources (13.1-13.2), all payable on the ordinary net-30/acceptance terms in Exhibit B's Payment Terms. Termination (11.1-11.2) is by non-renewal notice or for uncured material breach or insolvency, with no early-termination fee, minimum-fee shortfall, acceleration of remaining contract value or forfeiture on termination; post-termination payments under 11.3 are only continuing support/maintenance fees for services Corio elects to keep receiving. Section 9 further caps each party's liability at amounts actually paid by Corio, reinforcing that no stipulated or penal sum runs against us. The only true-up mechanics are the audit provisions in 4.4 (payment of an actual shortfall and reimbursement of examination cost on a >5% underpayment), which are compensatory audit terms rather than liquidated damages, and we note them for information only. No fallback early-termination-fee cap is needed because no Customer-payable liquidated amount exists.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-90da358d","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 9 LIMITATION OF LIABILITY.","rationale":"Section 9 caps liability mutually (\"either party\") and carves out Section 8 (indemnification), so mutuality and the indemnity carve-out are already met. However it fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) the cap is not 12 months' fees but only the fees paid for \"the transaction which the liability relates to\" in that period, which can be a small fraction of 12 months' fees and risks falling below the walk-away floor; and (ii) there are no carve-outs for breach of confidentiality (Section 10), gross negligence or willful misconduct — nothing elsewhere in the document supplies them. We therefore target the fallback with the shortest edit: delete the per-transaction narrowing and add the three missing carve-outs to the existing exception opener, leaving the rest of Section 9 (including the mutual consequential-damages waiver) untouched. Preferred items not pursued at this level (USD 1,000,000 floor, \"paid or payable\", data protection/security, fraud, IP infringement, payment-obligation exclusion) are noted only as upside.","proposal":"Remove the per-transaction narrowing of the 12-month fee cap and add carve-outs for confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-aad99306","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13 SHARED RESOURCES.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use covenant on Corio (our party). The only restrictions binding Corio are ordinary licence-scope and IP-protection limits: §2.7 bars copying/reverse engineering of Commerce One's Software, §12 bars distribution of escrowed Source Code, and §6.1 bars post-term use of Commerce One's Trademarks — none restrict what businesses Corio may operate or what products it may buy, build or resell. The Territory (§1.11) and Corio Market Segment (§1.3) provisions merely define the scope of the licences granted to Corio; they do not prohibit Corio from serving other segments with other products, and §1.3 expressly lets Corio retain customers that grow or are acquired above the threshold. The licences are nonexclusive (§2.1–2.4), Exhibit D's sales and marketing cooperation is expressly \"non-binding\", and §13.6 affirmatively preserves each party's right to develop independently. This meets the preferred position; no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-80528976","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"§ 11 TERM AND TERMINATION.","rationale":"Section 11.1 commits Corio to an initial five-year term with automatic one-year renewals, and Section 11.2 permits termination only for uncured material breach or insolvency; no convenience exit exists for Corio anywhere in the Agreement (the exits at p0050 and p0079 are acceptance-test and warranty remedies). The bargain therefore fails even the fallback, which requires a Customer convenience right on 60-90 days' notice. The 30-day non-renewal notice in 11.1 is natural-term non-renewal under RENEWAL and is not double-flagged here. New Section 11.4 states expressly that Corio is the customer under this Agreement and that the customer may terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' prior written notice, that Commerce One shall refund prepaid fees pro rata, and that Commerce One has no right to terminate for convenience during the initial five-year term or any renewal term - all four preferred elements in operative language. Lowercase \"customer\" is used so the grant does not collide with the defined term CUSTOMER(S) in Section 1.6. Sections 11.1-11.3 are untouched, and no Order Form or partial-termination language is added because this Agreement has no Order Form structure.","proposal":"Insert Section 11.4: the customer (Corio) may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and Commerce One has no convenience right during the initial or renewal terms.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-assign-ada12c9c","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14 MISCELLANEOUS.","rationale":"Section 14.1 is the only assignment provision, and no clause anywhere gives Commerce One a termination or re-pricing right on Corio's change of control (§ 11 termination triggers are breach and insolvency only), so we are outside walk-away territory. The clause already delivers two fallback elements mutually: successor assignment in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets without consent, and a consent requirement for all other assignments. It fails the fallback on two material terms: the consent requirement carries no reasonableness standard (so Commerce One could refuse an affiliate or other assignment arbitrarily), and the successor carve-out has no written-notice mechanic. We therefore propose the two shortest conforming edits to bring § 14.1 to the fallback level, leaving the mutual direct-competitor consent proviso and the null-and-void sentence untouched. We have not sought the preferred affiliate carve-out, since a no-consent affiliate exception is inconsistent with the fallback requirement that all non-successor assignments need consent.","proposal":"Add reasonableness standard to assignment consent and written notice for successor assignments in § 14.1.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-ae3291a5","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14 MISCELLANEOUS.","rationale":"Section 14.3 selects California law, which is acceptable at the fallback level, but the dispute forum is mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration in San Francisco rather than the corresponding California courts, so the fallback forum element fails on a material term (the arbitration seat is domestic, so this is not walk-away territory). We keep California law untouched and replace only the arbitration mechanic with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in San Francisco County, and conform the Section 12.2 escrow cross-reference so it no longer refers to arbitration under Section 14.3.","proposal":"Replace mandatory AAA arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the California courts; conform the escrow cross-reference.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-41c2ee89","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 3 2. GRANT OF RIGHTS.","rationale":"The Section 2 licences are perpetual and irrevocable (2.1) and fully paid up (2.2–2.4), and Section 14.1 permits assignment of the Agreement, and hence the licences, to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all related assets without consent, so the fallback successor-transfer element is met on its material terms (the direct-competitor carve-out is noted but not material here). However, no clause anywhere extends any licence to Corio's affiliates, and there is no defined \"Affiliates\" term or notice mechanic to add them, so the fallback affiliate element fails. We therefore propose the shortest fallback cure: a single provision extending the Section 2 licences to Corio's affiliates on written notice. Section 14.8 already lets Corio subcontract the Corio Services, and a grant to Corio reaches its authorised personnel, so no further change is sought.","proposal":"Extend the Section 2 licences to Corio affiliates on written notice","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-eea8b306","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"PRICING","rationale":"The agreement contains no most-favoured-nation, best-pricing, price-protection or right-to-match mechanic in either direction. The pricing and payment provisions (Exhibit B PRICING at p0152-p0154, REVENUE SHARING FEES at p0156-p0161, PAYMENT TERMS at p0165-p0168) and the Fees section (Sections 4.1-4.4) set fixed licence, MarketSite.net access, maintenance, revenue-share and implementation amounts, with no obligation on Corio to extend to Commerce One any terms given to third parties and no obligation to disclose or match third-party offers. Targeted searches for \"most favored/favourable\", \"no less favorable\", \"best/lowest pricing\", \"right to match\", \"first refusal\", \"comparable terms\" and \"similarly situated\" returned nothing, and the only other commercially adjacent provisions (Exhibit D sales and marketing cooperation, expressly non-binding, and Section 13 shared resources, which merely applies Commerce One's standard fees to Corio-requested personnel) impose no pricing-parity duty on us. This meets the preferred position that Customer has no MFN obligation benefiting Vendor, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-92500129","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 4 FEES.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no minimum purchase or volume commitment on Corio and no take-or-pay, shortfall-penalty or usage-cap mechanic. Corio's payment obligations are consideration for what it actually licenses and orders: the one-time BuySite licence fee due on Software Acceptance (§4.1, Exhibit B Payment Terms), the annual MarketSite.net access fee for the access it takes (§2.6, Exhibit B), the annual maintenance and support fee for support services (§4.2, which continues \"provided that Corio continues to pay\"), implementation fees on a time-and-materials basis capped at a maximum, and a percentage revenue share calculated on actual Application Management Revenue from live Corio Customers. Volume terms run in our favour rather than against us: Software Users are \"Unlimited\" and Corio may sublicense \"an unlimited number of Customers\". The only use of \"minimum\" affecting fees (Exhibit B §2.A, the 40-Authorized-User limitation) is a condition on a revenue-share exemption that benefits Corio, not a committed volume, and the \"shortfall\" reference in §4.4 is an audit true-up payable by whichever party underpaid. This sits at the preferred position, so no redline is warranted. We note only that the five-year initial term (§11.1) is terminable by Corio for breach or insolvency rather than at will; that is a term-length/exit point under the termination rules, not a minimum-commitment issue, and we do not flag it twice here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-283f3c6b","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13 SHARED RESOURCES.","rationale":"We searched the whole Agreement (Confidentiality § 10, Shared Resources § 13 including its personnel and Employee NDA covenants, Miscellaneous § 14, and Exhibit D's Personnel clause) for \"solicit\", \"hire\", \"induce\", \"recruit\" and \"employ or engage\": there is no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant anywhere. The only personnel-related covenants bind Commerce One (staffing and Employee NDA/Invention Agreement obligations) and impose no restriction on Corio's ability to solicit or hire. This meets the preferred position — Customer has no non-solicitation restriction — so no redline is required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-bf109f2c","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 11 TERM AND TERMINATION.","rationale":"Section 11.1 provides automatic renewal in successive one (1) year terms, exitable by either party (including Corio) on only thirty (30) days' written notice before the end of the initial term or any renewal term. The non-renewal notice window is 30 days, well inside the fallback ceiling of 60 days (and inside the preferred 30-day opt-out), and renewal terms are 12 months, so the walk-away triggers (windows over 90 days or automatic multi-year renewals) are not present. No renewal-period price uplift mechanic exists anywhere: Exhibit B fixes MarketSite.net and Maintenance and Support fees for \"Year 2-5, and beyond\", and Section 4.2 continues maintenance at the Exhibit B fees, so the conditional price-increase cap element is not triggered. The clause therefore sits at or above the fallback and is acceptable. The only shortfall against preferred wording is the absence of a Vendor reminder at least 60 days before renewal, which is a minor sub-element we note but do not redline; we would raise it only if a renewal reminder becomes commercially important.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-b2f8092e","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"medium","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 11 TERM AND TERMINATION.","rationale":"Sections 11 and 12 contain no transition-assistance or data-export mechanic. Section 11.3 only survives certain sections, preserves Corio's existing Customer licence rights and support (subject to continued payment), and requires each party to return or destroy the other's Confidential Information - it gives Commerce One no obligation to assist Corio with migration and no obligation to export Corio's data within a fixed period. The escrow provisions in Section 12 release Source Code only on limited Release Conditions and are not an exit/data-return right. We therefore insert a short provision at the fallback level: at least 90 days of transition assistance on any expiration or termination, and export of our data within 30 days.","proposal":"Insert transition assistance and data export obligation in Section 11","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-78977b85","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 8 7 WARRANTIES AND DISCLAIMER.","rationale":"Section 7.3 gives a real conformance-to-Documentation warranty for the Software and the MarketSite.net Service, and Section 7.4 adds a no-malicious-code warranty; Section 7.9's disclaimer is limited to implied warranties and does not swallow it. The remedies (commercially reasonable correction, free replacement, and a refund of all prepaid fees where the breach cannot be corrected) satisfy the fallback repair/replacement and refund elements, and the 60-day period already exceeds the 30-day services floor. 6. **Section 14.3 (GOVLAW):** retain California law; replace mandatory AAA arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in San Francisco County, and conform the Section 12.2 escrow cross-reference.

8. **Section 14.1 (ASSIGN):** add a reasonableness standard to the consent requirement and a written-notice mechanic for successor assignments; leave the mutual direct-competitor proviso and null-and-void sentence as drafted.
9. **Section 14 (INSURANCE):** insert the fallback clause (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber/privacy USD 2,000,000), with the fuller CGL/workers' compensation/certificate version available if Commerce One prefers it.
